title: How machine learning learns
examples: Can you explain the difference between training and testing data?
How does a machine actually learn the patterns from the examples?
What kind of data is best for training a machine?

explain.say: Today we will say how machines learn from data.

draw.text: ML Learning: Examples, Patterns, Training, Testing

explain.say: First we look at examples to teach the machine.
Next the machine looks for patterns within those examples.
Then the process of training uses these examples to build the model.
After training we use testing data to check its performance.
In real life you use this when filtering spam emails.

faq.q: What is the difference between training and testing data?
faq.a: Training data is what the machine learns from. Testing data is new data it has never seen before, used to check if it really learned.
asks: Why do we need two different sets of data?
How do I know if my model is good enough?

faq.q: Do I need a lot of examples to train a machine?
faq.a: Generally, yes, more examples help the machine find more accurate patterns. Too few examples can lead to poor learning.
asks: Is the amount of data important?
What if I only have a small dataset?

faq.q: What happens if my training data and testing data are similar?
faq.a: If they are too similar, the machine might just memorize the answers instead of learning the general rule. This is called overfitting.
asks: Can my machine cheat on the test?
What is overfitting in machine learning?

faq.q: Does the algorithm change when I change the data?
faq.a: The algorithm is the set of instructions, but the data influences how the algorithm adjusts its internal rules. The data guides the learning process.
asks: Does the data change the code?

faq.q: What is a pattern in this context?
faq.a: A pattern is a consistent relationship or trend that the machine notices across many examples. It is the underlying rule connecting the inputs to the correct outputs.
asks: Is a pattern just a coincidence?

facts: Machine learning requires labeled examples to learn effectively.
Training is the phase where the algorithm adjusts its parameters using data.
Testing data must be kept separate to ensure an unbiased evaluation.
Patterns are the rules or relationships the machine tries to identify.

quiz.say: A machine is shown 100 pictures of apples and 100 pictures of oranges. It learns what an apple looks like.
quiz.why: The process of showing the machine examples to learn is called training.

wrong.1: Testing only happens after the learning is finished.
wrong.2: Patterning is what happens inside the training, not the name of the whole process.
wrong.3: Example is the input, not the name of the learning stage.

quiz.say: You want to know if your spam filter works on brand new emails it has never seen before.
quiz.why: You must use unseen data, which is the definition of testing.

wrong.1: Training uses the data to build the filter itself.
wrong.2: This is the action, not the stage of checking the final result.
wrong.3: This just refers to the data, not the evaluation step.

quiz.say: If a machine learns that all dogs have floppy ears, but it fails on a picture of a pointy-eared dog, what did it miss?
quiz.why: It missed a broader pattern because it focused only on one feature.

wrong.0: More examples help, but the core issue is the type of pattern learned.
wrong.1: Testing only reveals the mistake; it doesn't fix the flawed pattern.
wrong.2: Time alone does not fix a flawed understanding of the pattern.
